newsitem.title: CANADA: Coca-Cola Beverages in environment dispute.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Beverages in environment dispute.

text.p: A Canadian environmental group said on Monday that they have launched a private legal action against Coca-Cola Beverages Ltd, charging the soft drink bottler with violating Ontario's environmental laws.
The Toronto Environmental Alliance (TEA) said its legal action was related to the government's requirement that 30 percent of soft drinks sold in Ontario be in refillable containers.
TEA said in a statement that less than two percent of Coca Cola Beverages' sales in the province are in refillable containers.
"Coke has been breaking this law since the day it was written and the government has made no effort to enforce it in years," TEA spokesman Gord Perks said in a statement.
Coca-Cola Beverages said the regulation is under review by the Ontario government because refillable containers are available, but consumers are simply not buying them.

"The regulation...says we have to sell 30 percent in refillable containers, but it does not make consumers buy them. That's why government itself says this is unenforceable," said Coca-Cola Beverages spokesman Tina Warren.
